consigna: One sustained spoken production of at least twelve minutes: deliver a talk on a contested public question — reporting what others have claimed, negotiating with an objector in the room, and sustaining emphasis across the argument, with one moment where the irony stops. With an audience or recorded alone.
requisitos: *Allegedly* and *reportedly* each used where the difference matters (week 38)
Naming the other side's real interest before they state it (week 39)
Two mixed conditionals reaching from past choices to the present (week 40)
Three rare inversion patterns, spread out, not stacked (week 41)
Disagreement located at a specific part of the claim (week 42)
Wry throughout, with one marked switch to sincerity (week 43)
microtareas: *Mon (10 min).* Skim all this year's corrections and note the one that never disappeared between weeks 2 and 45.
*Wed (5 min).* Write three sentences carrying an attribution, an inversion and a mixed conditional together.
*Fri (10 min).* Record the twelve minutes. Then check: is the year's correction back?
autochequeo: Did the attribution choices carry the weight they should?
Did naming their interest build trust or sound tactical?
Were the inversions spread out rather than stacked?
Is the correction that lasted all year still there?
promptCorreccion: This is a review of six skills at once: hedged attribution, interest-first negotiation, mixed conditionals, sustained inversion, located disagreement and controlled irony. (1) For each, say whether it is present and whether it is done well. (2) Name the one that consolidated least over the year. (3) Give me one sentence carrying three of them. Correct nothing outside these six areas. ---
